authorities.role: x86-64 locked operations and memory ordering
authorities.title: Intel 64 and IA-32 Software Developer Manual Volume 3A
Linux kernel sequence counters and sequential locks

family.raw_spinlock: FIFO ticket lock with try, unbounded, and bounded acquisition
family.interrupt_save_spinlock: ticket lock plus exact interrupt-enable and preemption-depth restoration
family.sleeping_mutex: fixed-capacity ownership-tracked handoff mutex with direct bounded priority donation
family.notification: fixed-capacity FIFO wait, wake-one, wake-all, timeout, and cancellation queue
family.reader_writer_lock: writer-ticketed and writer-preferred lock with try, bounded, and unbounded paths
family.sequence_lock: ticket-serialized writer and retrying stable-even reader protocol

bounds.timed_paths: caller-supplied finite attempt or monotonic-deadline bound

ownership_and_ordering.rank_rule: strictly increasing; same-rank nesting is rejected in PKLOCK1
ownership_and_ordering.graph: fixed five-node directed graph with precommit cycle detection and rollback
ownership_and_ordering.guard_binding: interrupt-save guards bind owner, rank, ticket, and originating lock address

execution_context.raw_spinlock: non-sleeping; caller owns interrupt and preemption discipline
execution_context.interrupt_save_spinlock: task context at interrupt depth zero and preemption depth zero
execution_context.sleeping_mutex: sleep-capable task context at interrupt depth zero and preemption depth zero
execution_context.notification_wait: sleep-capable task context at interrupt depth zero and preemption depth zero
execution_context.scheduler_bridge: PKSCHED1 ExternalLock block/wake reasons and one direct external priority donation slot

mutex_policy.selection: highest priority, FIFO within equal priority, oldest waiter after seven bypasses
mutex_policy.priority_inheritance: direct one-level maximum waiter priority only; no transitive chain claim
mutex_policy.handoff: ownership is reserved for the selected waiter until its exact wake receipt is claimed
mutex_policy.timeout: deadline-expired waiter is removed exactly once and donation is recomputed
mutex_policy.cancellation: named waiter is removed exactly once and donation is recomputed
mutex_policy.owner_death: all waiters receive OwnerDead and ownership/donation state is cleared
mutex_policy.starvation_bound: a continuously queued mutex waiter may be bypassed at most seven selections

memory_model.spin_handoff: release of owner and serving; acquire observation before claim
memory_model.reader_writer: acquire admission, release departure, and writer-pending exclusion of new readers
memory_model.sequence_lock: odd sequence brackets relaxed payload write; readers require equal acquire snapshots

live_profile.cleanup: shared aliases revoked before existing PKSMP5 shootdown, park, scrub, and release

failure_and_rollback.failed_spin_timeout: cancel exact ticket and skip it only while owner is clear
failure_and_rollback.foreign_irq_guard: reject before context or lock mutation
failure_and_rollback.failed_writer_reservation: remove waiting-writer state and cancel exact writer ticket
failure_and_rollback.invalid_sequence_state: reject before opening a writer interval
failure_and_rollback.counter_failure: preflight fallible diagnostics before ownership mutation where applicable
failure_and_rollback.panic_profile: selector failure emits PKLOCK1 denial and PanicCode 0x101E

progress_guarantees.raw_spinlock: FIFO among non-cancelled reserved tickets under continued execution of the current owner
progress_guarantees.sleeping_mutex: bounded bypass of seven for continuously queued waiters; direct donation only
progress_guarantees.reader_writer: queued writers exclude new readers; no wall-clock latency guarantee
progress_guarantees.sequence_lock: writers serialize; unbounded readers may retry indefinitely under continuous writes
progress_guarantees.system_progress: no wait-free, transitive-donation, NMI-safe, hotplug, general-SMP, or reclamation guarantee

nonclaims: PKLOCK1 does not implement RCU, hazard pointers, epoch reclamation, or ABA-safe object lifetime.
PKLOCK1 does not prove transitive priority donation, NMI-safe locking, arbitrary topology, hotplug, x2APIC, or non-x86 memory models.
The live profile exercises one shared ticket lock on one exact four-vCPU QEMU topology; host probes own sleeping, notification, reader-writer, and seqlock contention evidence.
No physical target, production authority, signature, N12 exit, release, or production-readiness claim is made.
